newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end bourse trade at lower levels.
newsitem.headline: German equities end bourse trade at lower levels.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade sharply lower on Tuesday amid what traders said was nervous market sentiment with no new data around to help lift spirits on the floor of the Frankfurt bourse.
The DAX index, which tracks bourse trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended down 23.63 points at 3,741.48 points, a fall of 0.63 percent. The June DAX futures contract was down six points at 3,744.
"There is a lot of nervousness around and a lot of it is related to the negotiations at the Amsterdam summit," one trader said of the European Union summit.
"A lot of the agreements in Amsterdam are being seen as posturing. It's all politics, and everyone thinks they are just trying to paper over the cracks in currency union," the trader said.
EU leaders, meeting in Amsterdam, on Monday agreed a resolution on employment to accompany the stability pact, the framework for keeping budgets tight under EMU.
In the share market on Tuesday, traders said that While there was a lot of movement going on, most of it was based on derivatives.
"There is the triple-witching on Friday, and there are a lot of U.S. figures this week, but basically I think this market needs a rest," the trader said.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed slightly lower overnight, down 0.13 percent at 7,772.09 points.
While such an inconclusive figure did not have a major impact on sentiment in Frankfurt, it did not provide the same levels of impetus as it has done in recent days.

Drugs group Schwarz Pharma was among the best performers in bourse trade after it received approval the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market its EDEX treatment for impotence in the United States.
Schwarz Pharma shares ended trade up two marks at 137 marks.
Shares in carbon and graphite maker SGL Carbon AG ended the day down 10.25 marks at 231.50 marks, after it said that it its U.S. unit had been presented with a class action lawsuit over price fixing.
